title: API versioning and compatibility
idea: Backward compatibility means a new release still works for every caller written against the old one; versioning lets you ship a breaking change beside it.
points: A published API is a contract: other code depends on its exact shape.
Adding is usually safe; removing, renaming or tightening anything breaks some caller.
Ship a breaking change as a new version that runs beside the old.
Mark old methods `@Deprecated`, tell callers, and remove them only after they move.

hero.caption: Most additions keep old callers working; an abstract method, a removal or a tightened rule needs a new version.

code.title: Evolving a Java interface
code.caption: Version 2 adds a priority overload as a `default` method. A class written for version 1 still compiles and gains it.

walk.text: The version 1 contract: one abstract method every implementer wrote.
Version 2 adds an overload with a body, built on the old method.
`LegacySms` was never edited, yet it now answers the new call too.
A newer class overrides the default to use priority its own way.
Old and new callers share one loop; nothing breaks.

code.title: Two versions side by side
code.caption: Version 2 renamed `capacity` to `seats`, a breaking change. Version 1 stays frozen, and both read one model.

walk.text: One current model; each version only maps it to its own shape.
The version 1 shape is frozen: the same field names until that version is retired.
Version 2 carries the rename and new fields.
An unknown version gets a stable error code, not a guess.

pitfalls: Never rename or remove a public field in place; add the new one, deprecate the old.
Do not add an abstract method to a published interface; give it a `default` body.
Make clients ignore unknown fields, or every additive change will break them.

quiz.q: Using `ApiEvolutionDemo`'s types, what does this print?
options: A compile error: LegacySms lacks the method
quiz.why: `LegacySms` inherits the `default` overload. It adds the `[!] ` prefix for `HIGH`, then calls the version 1 `send` that `LegacySms` implements.
quiz.code:
Notifier n = new LegacySms();
System.out.println(n.send("ada", "Hi", Priority.HIGH));

takeaway: Add freely, never break in place, and version what must break.
